messages:
Rachael (CS): Banyan opened a ticket reporting that their /v1/embeddings p99 jumped from typical ~200-300ms to ~3-4s after a marketing send this morning. They attached a curl + sample payload with a single request containing ~1.2k short texts.

Banyan Oncall: Confirmed — we kicked off a campaign at 09:10 UTC. Our app sees many timeouts and large tail latencies.

Miguel (SRE): Looking at telemetry now. I see a correlated p99 spike for tenant=banyan-prod on pool gpux-us-east-2c (pool-7). Investigating worker metrics and KV cache churn.

Maya (Ops): Worker histogram query shows one node (a100-40g-3) with high memcpy stalls and elevated queue depth during the window. Batch_count for that tenant spiked concurrently.

Noah (Eng): Note that rwd-embed-4k uses an attention kernel that is sensitive to batch aggregation. Large incoming batches of short sequences can cause the runtime's continuous batching to group a lot of inputs, increasing execution time and causing head-of-line blocking.

Miguel (SRE): Tried a staging repro: synthetic send of 1.2k inputs -> p95 ~380ms, p99 ~2.7s. Pattern matches customer report. Likely combination of large batch sizes + KV cache evictions when the working set flips.

Sam (Platform): Mitigation options available:
- enforce per-tenant concurrent-request cap (quick)
- reject oversized requests with 429 + Retry-After (non-transparent but explicit)
- route heavy batches to a reserved/dedicated pool (reservation)
- temporary priority allowlist for a billed campaign window

Rachael (CS): Customer asks for immediate mitigation so their app stops timing out. They prefer explicit 429s if necessary, and want the option to run the campaign without throttles if they can pay for isolation.

Miguel (SRE): Immediate plan of action:
1) Throttle banyan embeddings concurrency to 10 concurrent requests to lower queueing tail.
2) Soft-reject any single request with >800 items with 429 + Retry-After.
3) Offer a 1-hour reservation on pool-9 for the campaign window (charged).

Maya (Ops): Applying throttle patch to tenant config now:
{"tenant":"banyan-prod","embeddings_concurrency":"10","max_batch_size":"800"}

deploy-bot: config-update: tenant=banyan-prod key=throttle updated by Maya at 1864322150

Banyan Oncall: After throttle we see fewer app timeouts, p99 dropped to ~1.0-1.3s. 429s are acceptable for this run.

Maya (Ops): Created reservation id=res-banyan-1864322200 for pool-9 duration=3600s and assigned to banyan-prod.

deploy-bot: reservation-create: id=res-banyan-1864322200 pool=pool-9 duration=3600 assigned=banyan-prod

Rachael (CS): Gave reservation id to the customer and instructed them to include X-Reservation-ID header when sending. They will start in ~10 minutes.

Banyan Oncall: Launching with reservation header. Initial bursts show p99 ~360-400ms. Looks stable so far.

Miguel (SRE): Metric confirmation: reservation traffic is pinned to pool-9 and the heap/KV churn is isolated. Other tenants on pool-7 returned to baseline.

Noah (Eng): Root cause summary draft: oversized batch submissions from a single tenant + shared-pool KV cache thrash + continuous batching strategy lead to long tail latency for some requests.

Sam (Platform): Recommended long-term mitigations:
- server-side auto-splitting of very large input arrays into sub-batches to limit head-of-line blocking
- auto-provisioning of short reservations when campaign-like patterns detected (requires billing/consent)
- per-pool alerts when a tenant consumes >X% of pool concurrency

Maya (Ops): Cleanup plan: remove the temporary throttle at 1864325800 (reservation end) unless customer asks for extension.

Miguel (SRE): Added a runbook snippet for "embedding large-batch campaign" with detection and mitigation steps. Will update with any postmortem details.

Rachael (CS): I'll follow up with the customer on best-practice batch sizes, scheduling guidance, and a formal quote for reservation pricing. Will close the support ticket after PM + pricing sent.

Banyan Oncall: Thanks everyone for the quick help! :rocket:

(keeping thread open 24h to monitor)
